Note.description: A page in the garden — a paper summary, a symptom log, a session note, an index. The only type that owns prose on the site.

Session.description: A dated event in the case: a self-administered test, a therapy conversation, a clinical appointment, a deliberate journalling pass. The unit of 'what we did and when'.

Symptom.description: An experienced pattern being tracked — described phenomenologically, not diagnostically.

Instrument.description: A measurement tool: a screener, a questionnaire, a cognitive task, a lab panel, a wearable metric.

Finding.description: A concrete result produced by a Session — a score, a clinician's observation, a lab value. Facts about the case, distinct from what they might mean.

Intervention.description: Something deliberately changed and tracked over time: medication, sleep protocol, therapy, exercise, caffeine, environment.

Mechanism.description: A named cognitive/neural construct the notebook reuses: response inhibition, statistical learning, mind-wandering, executive function.

Hypothesis.description: A load-bearing assertion the notebook is trying to defend or falsify. Never a diagnosis — always something that can be pressure-tested.

Question.description: An open problem the notebook is working on; can gate a Note, a Hypothesis, or a next Session.

Paper.description: An external work cited: journal article, preprint, book, clinical guideline.

Tension.description: A competing-explanation or trade-off held open on purpose — e.g. ADHD vs. anxiety as the source of the same symptom. Reified so it cannot quietly resolve itself.

Status.description: Lifecycle status (a hub-transit type: reachable but never traversed through).

partOf.description: Note belongs to a parent Note (section index).

covers.description: This note is where the thing is written up.

measures.description: Instrument is designed to measure this symptom domain or construct.

administeredIn.description: Instrument was administered during this session.

observedIn.description: Symptom was reported/observed in this session.

precedes.description: Session comes before another session — the timeline spine.

mayExplain.description: Candidate explanation for an experience or result. HYPOTHETICAL by construction — never a diagnosis.

affects.description: Intervention is being tracked for its effect on this.

derivesFrom.description: X is built on / specialises Y.

documentedIn.description: The case fact is written up in this note.

definedIn.description: Mechanism has its primary development in this note.

cites.description: Note cites a paper (a deliberate act, never inferred from prose).

dependsOn.description: Hypothesis rests on another hypothesis, on a question resolving a particular way, or on a finding holding up.

supports.description: Paper supports this hypothesis/mechanism. The edge carries the verbatim quote + page locator + confidence + rationale, so a fact and its justification travel together.

pressureTests.description: Paper challenges/qualifies this hypothesis/mechanism. Same evidence payload.

confounds.description: A rival explanation that must be ruled out before the hypothesis can stand. The honesty predicate of this ontology.

tensionWith.description: In unresolved tension with (both endpoints stay live).

supersedes.description: Replaces a prior version — later screening supersedes an earlier one, a revised hypothesis supersedes its draft.

flagsOpenQuestion.description: Flags an open question the node rests on.

wikiLinks.description: Wiki-style link parsed from prose. Navigation only — kept out of the argument graph.

structural.description: Where a thing sits: containment, coverage, what measures what.

temporal.description: The case timeline: what happened when, in what order, and what it produced.

causal.description: What might explain or affect what. Always hypothetical in this corpus.

provenance.description: Where a thing came from: which note records it, which paper, which author.

dialectical.description: What is contested: evidence, confounds, contradictions, supersession, open questions.

weak.description: Casual cross-links for navigation only — deliberately kept out of the argument graph.

nodes.label: 2026-07-26 — ASRS v1.1 self-screening & reflection
nodes.summary: Took the ASRS v1.1 (WHO-developed adult ADHD screener) and reflected on presentations and the 'calm outside, churning inside' pattern with a therapist who is themselves diagnosed with ADHD.

nodes.label: ASRS v1.1 (Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale)
nodes.summary: 18-item WHO-developed screener. Part A (6 items, cutoff ≥4) determines the screen; Part B (12 items) characterises symptom load. Deliberately tuned for sensitivity, so a positive screen is a reason to evaluate, not a diagnosis.

nodes.label: Cognitive Trade-off Task (ASRT + Go/No-Go)
nodes.summary: The paradigm used by Horváth et al. 2026: an Alternating Serial Reaction Time Task carrying a hidden probabilistic sequence (statistical learning) with an embedded Go/No-Go component (response inhibition), so both are measured at once rather than in isolation.

nodes.label: Continuous performance test (CPT / QbTest)
nodes.summary: Sustained-attention task requiring responses to targets and withholding to non-targets over a long, monotonous session. Indexes vigilance, inhibition and reaction-time variability; sensitive to ADHD but not diagnostically specific.

nodes.label: Stop-signal / go-no-go task
nodes.summary: Measures the ability to cancel an already-initiated response (the stop-signal reaction time) — the cleanest isolation of response inhibition.

nodes.label: Delay-discounting / choice-delay task
nodes.summary: Choices between smaller-sooner and larger-later rewards, quantifying how steeply delayed value is discounted — the motivational/delay-aversion pathway.

nodes.label: Working-memory task (n-back / span)
nodes.summary: n-back and complex-span paradigms indexing the capacity to hold and manipulate information over short intervals.

nodes.label: SWAN rating scale
nodes.summary: Strengths and Weaknesses of ADHD-symptoms and Normal-behavior scale: rates each symptom on a symmetric −3 to +3 range so both tails are measured, yielding roughly normally distributed population scores.

nodes.label: CAARS (Conners Adult ADHD Rating Scales)
nodes.summary: Norm-referenced adult ADHD rating scale scored as T-scores against a population sample; the T≥65 cutoff trades sensitivity for specificity.

nodes.label: BAARS-IV (Barkley Adult ADHD Rating Scale)
nodes.summary: DSM-anchored adult ADHD rating scale with current and childhood-symptom subscales, self- or observer-administered.

nodes.label: PID-5 (Disinhibition domain)
nodes.summary: Dimensional maladaptive-trait inventory; its Disinhibition domain (and Distractibility facet) places a person on the HiTOP disinhibited-externalizing spectrum rather than in the ADHD category.

nodes.label: ASRS v1.1 Part A: 4/6 — positive screen
nodes.summary: Landed exactly at the cutoff on the six-item screener that determines the result. Part A is the most predictive component. Screening only — not a diagnosis.

nodes.label: ASRS v1.1 Part B: 6/12 supplementary symptoms
nodes.summary: Part B has no threshold; it describes which symptoms show up. Six indicates a meaningful additional symptom load, backing the Part A result.

nodes.label: No formal diagnosis as of 2026-07-26
nodes.summary: State of the record: a positive screen only. Everything downstream is hypothesis.

nodes.label: Disruptive internal state — calm outside, churning inside
nodes.summary: Outwardly calm and not fidgety, but a racing, unsettled mind — the DSM 'driven as if by a motor' item experienced mentally rather than behaviourally. The often-missed pattern in inattentive-leaning adults.

nodes.label: Inattentive pattern — sustaining focus, distractibility
nodes.summary: Consistent with a positive ASRS Part A and a lean toward the inattentive presentation.

nodes.label: Acting before thinking / impulsivity items
nodes.summary: Endorsed on the ASRS; the axis the Horváth paper probes directly via response inhibition.

nodes.label: Response inhibition
nodes.summary: The capacity to withhold a prepared response — indexed by No-Go accuracy. Consistently weaker at higher ADHD-trait load, even below clinical thresholds.

nodes.label: Statistical learning
nodes.summary: Implicit extraction of environmental regularities — the habit-learning system. Indexed by faster responses to high-probability triplets.

nodes.label: Inhibition–learning antagonism (competition hypothesis)
nodes.summary: The trade-off in which weaker inhibitory control normally buys stronger statistical learning. The paper's central object of study.

nodes.label: ADHD as a trait continuum
nodes.summary: The dimensional view: ADHD-like traits are distributed across the general population, and neurocognitive shifts appear before symptoms reach clinical significance. The frame that makes a screening score meaningful without a diagnosis.

nodes.label: Cue as motivational magnet (sign-tracking)
nodes.summary: Borrowed from animal sign-tracker/goal-tracker work: at high trait load the cue itself captures behaviour and top-down systems cannot override it — the authors' proposed reason the learning advantage breaks down.

nodes.label: Mind-wandering
nodes.summary: Spontaneous shift of attention from external demands to internally generated thought; offered as a second, transdiagnostic candidate mechanism.

nodes.label: Anxiety-driven arousal
nodes.summary: Chronic anxious arousal produces internal churn that is phenomenologically near-identical to internal hyperactivity, and frequently co-occurs with ADHD. The single most important thing to rule out here.

nodes.label: Sleep debt / disrupted sleep
nodes.summary: Insufficient or fragmented sleep degrades attention and produces restlessness — a mimic that must be excluded before attributing symptoms to ADHD.

nodes.label: Mood disturbance (depression / chronic stress)
nodes.summary: Depression and chronic stress produce concentration difficulty and inner agitation. Another mimic on the differential.

nodes.label: Sustained attention / vigilance
nodes.summary: The capacity to maintain attention on a task over time. A mechanism-level axis, indexed by continuous performance tests; lapses show up as reaction-time variability.

nodes.label: Working memory
nodes.summary: Holding and manipulating information over short intervals. One of the dissociable neurocognitive routes to ADHD-like presentation; indexed by n-back and complex-span tasks.

nodes.label: Reward processing / delay aversion
nodes.summary: The motivational pathway: an aversion to waiting and steeper discounting of delayed rewards. Partly independent of the inhibitory route; indexed by delay-discounting paradigms.

nodes.label: Arousal / state regulation
nodes.summary: Regulation of physiological and cognitive arousal. The axis ADHD shares most with its mimics — anxiety, sleep debt and mood all perturb it, which is why they overlap ADHD at the phenotype.

nodes.label: Reaction-time variability
nodes.summary: Intra-individual variability in response speed — a robust and heavily replicated ADHD marker, but not specific to ADHD relative to other clinical groups.

nodes.label: Temporal processing / timing
nodes.summary: Perception and reproduction of time intervals. A third dissociable component in multiple-pathway models, independent of inhibition and delay aversion.

nodes.label: My disruptive internal state is ADHD-driven rather than anxiety-, sleep-, or mood-driven
nodes.summary: The load-bearing personal hypothesis. Three rival mechanisms confound it and none has been ruled out; it cannot advance until the internal state is described concretely.

nodes.label: My ASRS result places me on the ADHD trait continuum rather than in a yes/no category
nodes.summary: Framing rather than diagnosis: a Part A score at the cutoff situates me somewhere on a spectrum the literature treats dimensionally.

nodes.label: ADHD's latent structure is dimensional (a continuum), not a discrete taxon
nodes.summary: Taxometric analyses of ADHD symptom data repeatedly fail to recover a category boundary and instead fit a continuous latent dimension. Contested: some analyses recover categorical structure within clinical samples.

nodes.label: Clinical ADHD is the quantitative extreme of a continuously distributed, heritable trait
nodes.summary: Twin and molecular-genetic evidence that the same aetiological factors operate across the whole symptom range, so the diagnosis marks a position on a continuum rather than a distinct condition.

nodes.label: The DSM symptom-count threshold is an arbitrary cut on a continuum with no natural breakpoint
nodes.summary: Impairment and quality of life decline linearly across the trait range with no discontinuity, so any diagnostic cutoff is a clinical convention. Held live by the counter-argument that unbounded threshold-lowering risks overdiagnosis and net harm.

nodes.label: Major dimensional frameworks (RDoC, HiTOP, the p-factor) place ADHD within continuous, transdiagnostic spectra
nodes.summary: The leading post-DSM classification programmes are all dimensional and locate ADHD on graded spectra (externalizing/disinhibition, general psychopathology) rather than in a discrete box.

nodes.label: A positive ASRS screen warrants a full clinical evaluation
nodes.summary: The actionable claim. Holds regardless of how the ADHD-vs-mimics question resolves — the evaluation is what resolves it.

nodes.label: Higher ADHD-like traits are associated with weaker response inhibition
nodes.summary: Research-side claim, replicated by the Horváth study in a non-clinical sample and under dual-task load.

nodes.label: Rising ADHD-trait load progressively flattens the inhibition–learning trade-off
nodes.summary: The paper's core result: the compensatory learning advantage that normally accompanies weak inhibition breaks down at the high end of the trait continuum.

nodes.label: Inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are distinct but strongly correlated, not orthogonal
nodes.summary: At the phenotype level the two DSM domains share a dominant general factor (latent r ≈ .68–.78); a bifactor structure fits best, so the domains are oblique rather than independent axes.

nodes.label: Rating-based and task-based measures of the same construct are only weakly related
nodes.summary: Questionnaire and performance measures of executive function correlate at about median r = .19 and assess different levels of cognition — so the two instrument families are near-orthogonal, not interchangeable.

nodes.label: ADHD arises through dissociable neurocognitive pathways, present in some individuals but not others
nodes.summary: Inhibitory, delay/reward and timing deficits are independent components whose co-occurrence is no greater than chance, and no single deficit is universal — the mechanism level is genuinely near-orthogonal.

nodes.label: No single instrument is diagnostic; valid assessment is multi-method across levels
nodes.summary: Ratings and tasks disagree, the best objective tasks are not decisive, and robust markers like reaction-time variability are not ADHD-specific — so discriminating ADHD (and its mimics) requires a multi-method evaluation, not one measure.

nodes.label: What does the 'disruptive internal state' actually consist of?
nodes.summary: Racing/jumping thoughts, a physical-but-invisible wound-up feeling, an inability to ever relax, or something else. These feel similar from the inside but point in different directions.
nodes.nextStep: Journal concrete examples as they happen, with time of day and context.

nodes.label: Is the internal restlessness driven by ADHD, anxiety, sleep, mood, or a combination?
nodes.summary: The differential. A good evaluator traces the symptom to its source rather than assuming the ADHD thread.
nodes.nextStep: Bring the differential explicitly to the evaluation; don't let it collapse into a single label.

nodes.label: Where would my ASRS score fall relative to the Horváth sample?
nodes.summary: The paper's sample scored M = 31.66, SD = 10.04 on the 18-item ASRS. My record currently stores Part A/Part B counts, not the summed dimensional score — so the comparison can't yet be made.
nodes.nextStep: Retain the item-level ASRS responses and compute the summed score.

nodes.label: What is the right next clinical step, and with whom?
nodes.summary: GP referral, psychologist, or psychiatrist — and what to bring to make the appointment productive.
nodes.nextStep: Draft a one-page summary for a clinician from the diagnostics note and the symptom log.

nodes.label: ADHD-like traits reshape the balance between inhibitory control and predictive processes
nodes.summary: n = 226 non-clinical sample; Cognitive Trade-off Task measuring response inhibition and statistical learning simultaneously; ADHD traits measured dimensionally with the ASRS v1.1.

nodes.label: Annual Research Review: Categories versus dimensions in the classification and conceptualisation of child and adolescent mental disorders
nodes.venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 53(5):469–489
nodes.summary: Canonical review of the category-vs-dimension question in child psychopathology; summarises the ADHD taxometric studies (Haslam 2006, Marcus & Barry 2011) and concludes ADHD is best modelled as a continuum.

nodes.label: Understanding attention deficit hyperactivity disorder as a continuum
nodes.summary: Clinician-facing review arguing ADHD lacks a taxon; neuropsychological performance varies linearly with symptom load with no discontinuity, creating uncertainty about where any intervention threshold should sit.

nodes.label: Does Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Have a Dimensional Latent Structure? A Taxometric Analysis
nodes.summary: Taxometric analysis of the NICHD sample finding a dimensional latent structure for inattention, hyperactivity/impulsivity and ADHD overall, with stronger validity than dichotomous models.

nodes.label: Genetics of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
nodes.summary: Review of ADHD genetics; twin and molecular evidence that clinical ADHD is the extreme of a continuous, heritable distribution with shared aetiology across the full symptom range.

nodes.label: Discovery of the first genome-wide significant risk loci for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder
nodes.summary: First well-powered ADHD GWAS; strong concordance with GWAS of quantitative population symptom measures supports clinical ADHD as an extreme expression of continuous heritable traits.

nodes.label: The World Health Organization Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS): a short screening scale for use in the general population
nodes.summary: Development of the ASRS; optimal scoring is an unweighted symptom sum (a dimensional score), with a 6-item Part A retained as a fast screener.

nodes.label: SWAN Scale for ADHD Trait-Based Genetic Research: A Validity and Polygenic Risk Study
nodes.venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 60(9):988–997
nodes.summary: Validates the SWAN, a symmetric strengths-to-weaknesses rating that yields roughly normally distributed ADHD-trait scores; argues dichotomising a continuous trait into case/control loses statistical power.

nodes.label: The Factor Structure of ADHD – Different Models, Analyses and Informants in a Bifactor Framework
nodes.venue: Journal of Psychopathology and Behavioral Assessment, 39(1):92–102
nodes.summary: Supports a bifactor structure for ADHD: a dominant general factor plus weak specific inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity factors.

nodes.label: Research Domain Criteria (RDoC): Toward a New Classification Framework for Research on Mental Disorders
nodes.summary: Founding RDoC commentary; reorganises psychopathology around functional dimensions studied across their full range, including executive- and impulse-control constructs central to ADHD.

nodes.label: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP): A Dimensional Alternative to Traditional Nosologies
nodes.summary: Dimensional classification framework that places ADHD within the (disinhibited) externalizing super-spectrum rather than as a discrete category.

nodes.label: The p Factor: One General Psychopathology Factor in the Structure of Psychiatric Disorders?
nodes.summary: Finds psychopathology is best captured by a single general 'p' dimension paralleling g; ADHD loads via the externalizing pole, reinforcing a graded liability model.

nodes.label: Is ADHD a Dimension or a Category? What Does the Relationship Between ADHD Traits and Psychosocial Quality of Life Tell Us?
nodes.summary: Psychosocial quality of life declines linearly with ADHD-trait level, with no non-linear breakpoint at the high end — direct support for a dimensional model over a category.

nodes.label: Subthreshold Autism and ADHD: A Brief Narrative Review for Frontline Clinicians
nodes.summary: Narrative review synthesising taxometric, impairment and threshold evidence; documents that sub-threshold ADHD carries wide-ranging functional impairment relative to unaffected peers.

nodes.label: Overdiagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Scoping Review
nodes.summary: Scoping review of 334 studies finding convincing evidence that ADHD is overdiagnosed; for milder cases the harms of diagnosis may outweigh the benefits — a caution against unbounded threshold-lowering.

nodes.label: Childhood attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder as an extreme of a continuous trait: a quantitative genetic study of 8,500 twin pairs
nodes.venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 53(1):73–80
nodes.summary: Flagship twin study reporting near-identical group heritability at diagnostic and screening cutoffs — ADHD as the quantitative extreme of a continuous trait.

nodes.label: Dimensional and Categorical Approaches to Understanding Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: New Frontiers in Translational Research
nodes.venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 3(8):652–653
nodes.summary: Counter-point to the dimensional consensus: reports taxometric outcomes more consistent with a categorical structure within ADHD samples and a dimensional structure in typically developing groups.

nodes.label: The factor structure of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in schoolchildren
nodes.venue: medRxiv preprint (later Research in Developmental Disabilities)
nodes.summary: Reports the latent correlation between the inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity factors (0.78 school / 0.68 clinical) and finds a bifactor model — strong general factor plus weak specific factors — fits best.

nodes.label: Practitioner Review: Do performance-based measures and ratings of executive function assess the same construct?
nodes.venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 54(2):131–143
nodes.summary: Review of 20 studies finding rating-based and performance-based measures of executive function correlate only weakly (median r = .19) and assess different underlying constructs.

nodes.label: Causal heterogeneity in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: do we need neuropsychologically impaired subtypes?
nodes.summary: Argues that group neuropsychological deficits in ADHD reflect only a subgroup — for any given mechanism, only a subset of behaviourally defined cases is impaired.

nodes.label: Beyond the dual pathway model: evidence for the dissociation of timing, inhibitory, and delay-related impairments in ADHD
nodes.venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 49(4):345–355
nodes.summary: Finds inhibitory, temporal-processing and delay-related deficits are independent neuropsychological components whose co-occurrence in ADHD is no greater than chance — dissociable pathways.

nodes.label: Reaction time variability in ADHD: a meta-analytic review of 319 studies
nodes.summary: Meta-analysis establishing greater reaction-time variability in ADHD (g = 0.76 children, 0.46 adults) while showing it is not specific to ADHD relative to other clinical groups.

nodes.label: The clinical utility of the continuous performance test and objective measures of activity for diagnosing and monitoring ADHD in children: a systematic review
nodes.summary: Systematic review finding mixed, non-decisive evidence for using continuous performance tests to support ADHD diagnosis and medication decisions.

nodes.label: A review of the validity of laboratory cognitive tasks used to assess symptoms of ADHD
nodes.summary: Concludes that even the best-supported cognitive tasks (CPT, choice-delay, stop-signal) need further validation before use beyond experimental purposes.

nodes.label: Validity of the executive function theory of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analytic review
nodes.summary: Landmark meta-analysis: executive-function deficits in ADHD are of moderate effect size and not universal — neither necessary nor sufficient.

nodes.label: A comprehensive assessment of memory, delay aversion, timing, inhibition, decision making and variability in ADHD
nodes.summary: For each cognitive domain, only a minority of children with ADHD (roughly 18–36%) show a deficit — quantifying neurocognitive heterogeneity across six pathways.

nodes.label: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Monetary Delay Discounting: A Meta-Analysis of Case-Control Studies
nodes.venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 1(4):316–325
nodes.summary: Meta-analysis finding individuals with ADHD discount delayed monetary rewards more steeply than controls — the motivational/reward pathway.

nodes.label: A review of behavioural rating scales for the assessment of ADHD among adults in research
nodes.summary: Reviews adult ADHD rating scales (incl. CAARS, BAARS-IV); notes scales should not be the sole basis for diagnosis and that combining interviews, CPTs and scales maximises accuracy.

nodes.label: Diagnosing ADHD
nodes.venue: CHADD — National Resource Center on ADHD (CDC cooperative agreement)
nodes.summary: Patient-facing clinical guidance stating there is no single test for ADHD and that a comprehensive, multi-source evaluation is required.

nodes.label: Unraveling the optimum latent structure of ADHD: evidence supporting ICD and HiTOP frameworks
nodes.summary: Locates ADHD within HiTOP as dimensions (inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity) under the disinhibited externalizing spectrum rather than as a single category.

nodes.label: The same internal restlessness fits ADHD and anxiety equally well
nodes.summary: Held open deliberately. Internal hyperactivity and anxious arousal are near-indistinguishable from the inside, they co-occur often, and depression/stress/sleep produce similar churn. Nothing in the record currently discriminates between them.

nodes.label: The evidence base doesn't obviously generalise to me
nodes.summary: The Horváth sample was 226 university students, 81% women, mean age 21.4, tested online without supervision. The authors themselves caution about generalisability to men and across the lifespan — so the dimensional framing is borrowed, not measured, for my case.

nodes.label: Is ADHD truly dimensional, or does it retain categorical structure?
nodes.summary: The dominant taxometric, quantitative-genetic and impairment evidence favours a continuum, but some taxometric analyses recover categorical structure within ADHD samples (Fassbender 2018) and reviews warn that dimensional thinking can license overdiagnosis (Kazda 2021). A clinically justified action threshold is still required. Held open on purpose.

edges.quote: Taken together, these analyses suggested that ADHD is best modelled as a continuum in both children and adolescents, thus supporting the genetic and other evidence that suggests a dimensional structure and multifactorial aetiology.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the fetched open-access full text; the canonical review's summary conclusion across three ADHD taxometric studies (Haslam 2006; Marcus & Barry 2011).

edges.quote: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder does not appear to have a taxon.
edges.pageApprox: 'Lack of evidence for a discrete category', para 1
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the cfp.ca full text; a taxon is the formal signature of a real category boundary, and ADHD lacks one.

edges.quote: Taxometric analysis outcomes were more consistent with a categorical structure to the data in the group with ADHD and a dimensional structure in the typically developing group.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text; the mandatory rival — a taxometric result recovering categorical (not dimensional) structure within the ADHD group.

edges.quote: Both studies suggest that the diagnosis of ADHD is the extreme of a continuous distribution of ADHD symptoms in the population and that the etiologic factors involved in the disorder also account for the full range of symptoms.
edges.pageApprox: 'Evidence for heritability from family, adoption, and twin studies'
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the Nature full text; twin evidence that the same aetiology operates across the whole symptom range, not just at the tail.

edges.quote: Strong concordance with GWAS of quantitative population measures of ADHD symptoms supports that clinical diagnosis of ADHD is an extreme expression of continuous heritable traits.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the fetched abstract; molecular (common-variant) evidence for the same conclusion as the twin work.

edges.quote: Psychosocial QoL gradually declines in a linear manner as ADHD trait levels increase providing further support for a dimensional model.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; impairment rises linearly with trait level with no non-linear breakpoint, so any cutoff is a convention rather than a natural join.

edges.quote: the lack of discontinuity in the distribution of such traits in the population creates great uncertainty as to what thresholds should prompt explicit intervention.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the cfp.ca full text; the practical consequence of continuity for where an intervention threshold should sit.

edges.quote: A review and meta-analysis showed high risks for negative outcomes in a wide range of non-overlapping functional domains in CYP with subthreshold ADHD, compared to children with no ADHD symptoms, including significantly higher rates of family dysfunction, cognitive impairment, executive dysfunction, interpersonal and school deficits, temperament problems, psychiatric comorbidity, and juvenile delinquency.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the MDPI full text; sub-threshold cases carry real impairment, undercutting the idea that the threshold separates impaired from unimpaired. Medium because it is a narrative review reporting a secondary meta-analysis.

edges.quote: In this systematic scoping review of 334 published studies in children and adolescents, convincing evidence was found that ADHD is overdiagnosed in children and adolescents. For individuals with milder symptoms in particular, the harms associated with an ADHD diagnosis may often outweigh the benefits.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text; the counter-argument that a continuum does not license unbounded threshold-lowering — a clinically justified action threshold is still required.

edges.quote: ADHD is now widely considered to be the extreme end of widely distributed, quantitative traits (Larsson, Anckarsater, Rastam, Chang, & Lichtenstein, 2012; Levy, Hay, McStephen, Wood, & Waldman, 1997). Although diagnostic categories are useful in clinical practice, dichotomizing continuously distributed traits into case/control reduces statistical power in research.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the open-access SickKids manuscript; states the continuum framing and the measurement rationale behind dimensional instruments like the SWAN.

edges.quote: Optimal scoring to predict clinical syndrome classifications was to sum unweighted dichotomous responses across all 18 ASRS questions.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the Harvard HCP copy; the ASRS — the instrument the personal record uses — is optimally read as a summed dimensional score, not a category. Medium because the quote concerns scoring rather than the trait's population structure directly.

edges.quote: The traditional externalizing dimension captures comorbidity among substance use disorders, oppositional defiant disorder (ODD), conduct disorder, adult antisocial behavior, intermittent explosive disorder (IED), and attention-deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the UNT-hosted copy of the published paper; HiTOP places ADHD within a continuous externalizing spectrum.

edges.quote: While maintaining a clear focus on overt psychopathology, investigators will be encouraged to explicate the full range of a given dimension to develop thresholds for different types of interventions and identify early opportunities for preventive interventions.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the publisher full text; RDoC's core dimensional logic, applied to the executive- and impulse-control constructs central to ADHD.

edges.quote: Psychiatric disorders were initially explained by three higher-order factors (Internalizing, Externalizing, and Thought Disorder) but explained even better with one General Psychopathology dimension.
edges.rationale: Verbatim from the publisher abstract; the p-factor model on which ADHD loads via the externalizing pole. Medium because the ADHD-specific loading was not confirmable verbatim from primary text.

edges.quote: The correlation between IN and HYIMP=0.78.
edges.rationale: Latent two-factor correlation (0.78 school / 0.68 clinical) shows inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are distinct but strongly correlated — oblique, not orthogonal — verified against the fetched full-text PDF.

edges.quote: Only 68 (24%) of the 286 relevant correlations reported in these studies were statistically significant, and the overall median correlation was only .19.
edges.rationale: Verified against author-hosted full text; the two instrument families measuring the 'same' construct barely converge — method variance dominates.

edges.quote: For ADHD patients, the co-occurrence of inhibitory, temporal processing and delay-related deficits was no greater than expected by chance with substantial groups of patients showing only one problem.
edges.rationale: Verified via the ERIC full abstract; the mechanistic components are statistically independent — the core orthogonality-at-the-mechanism-level result.

edges.quote: future theory and research give more consideration to the probability that only a subset of behaviorally defined children will have a deficit in a given neurocognitive mechanism believed to contribute to the disorder.
edges.rationale: Verified against fetched text; the corollary of dissociability — no single mechanism is universal, so several must be sampled.

edges.quote: children/adolescents (Hedges' g = 0.76) and adults (g = 0.46) with ADHD demonstrated greater RT variability relative to TD groups.
edges.rationale: Verified against the FSU full-text PDF; establishes RT variability as a robust, heavily replicated ADHD marker.

edges.quote: Comparison with clinical control groups reveals that RT variability is not specific to ADHD.
edges.rationale: Verified full text; the mandatory caution — even the most robust task marker cannot discriminate ADHD from other clinical conditions, so no single measure is diagnostic.

edges.quote: the CPT, C-DT, and the SST had the most support, yet further efforts to evaluate the validity of these measures are needed before they can be used for more than experimental purposes.
edges.rationale: Verified against SpringerLink; even the best-supported cognitive tasks are not validated for clinical decision-making.

edges.quote: There were mixed findings with regard to the use of CPTs to assess and manage medication, with contrasting evidence on their ability to support clinical decision-making.
edges.rationale: Verified against the Springer record; systematic review shows the leading objective measure is not decisive on its own.

edges.quote: Although behavioural rating scales should not be relied upon solely to clinically diagnose adult ADHD, they are often regarded as a valuable tool in research settings.
edges.rationale: Verified full text (preprint); the rating side of the same point — scales alone are not diagnostic, multi-method is needed.

edges.quote: There is no single test to diagnose ADHD. Therefore, a comprehensive evaluation is necessary to establish a diagnosis, rule out other causes, and determine the presence or absence of co-existing conditions.
edges.rationale: Verified against the CHADD page; the plainest statement of the multi-method conclusion, and the direct guidance for the personal next clinical step.

edges.quote: Below this are six spectra (somatoform, internalizing, thought disorder, disinhibited externalizing, antagonistic externalizing, and detachment).
edges.rationale: Verified full text; specifies the HiTOP spectra under which ADHD's dimensions (IA, HY, IMP) sit — the measurement-level realisation of the nosology axis.

edges.quote: We found that higher ADHD-like traits were associated with poorer response inhibition, confirming previous research.
edges.rationale: Direct statement of the primary result in a non-clinical sample (n = 226), replicating a hallmark finding below diagnostic thresholds.

edges.quote: this learning advantage progressively diminished across the ADHD trait continuum, becoming markedly reduced in individuals with high symptom prevalence
edges.rationale: The paper's core claim; backed in Results by a significant three-way interaction (No-Go performance x ASRS x Triplet Type, F(1, 13046.16) = 4.36, p = .037).

edges.quote: a condition understood to exist along a continuum of traits in the general population
edges.rationale: States the dimensional framing the whole design rests on — the reason a screening score is meaningful without a diagnosis.

edges.quote: we uncovered an antagonistic relationship between inhibition and statistical learning: weaker inhibitory control was linked to enhanced learning of environmental regularities
edges.rationale: Simple-effects analysis: learning effect b = -9.40 at low No-Go accuracy vs. b = -2.92 at high accuracy, all pairwise contrasts significant.

edges.quote: the No-Go signal may function as a motivational magnet that triggers an automatic response
edges.rationale: Explicitly framed by the authors as a hypothesised interpretation borrowed from animal sign-tracker research, not a measured mechanism.

edges.quote: Another angle of interpretation emerges from research on mind wandering, the spontaneous shift of attention from external demands to internally generated thought
edges.rationale: Offered as a secondary, transdiagnostic candidate; not measured in this study. Relevant here only because it is the closest published construct to the 'churning inside' description.

edges.quote: our sample consisted primarily of university students, which resulted in a narrow age range and high educational attainment. While this population is common in cognitive research, it may not be fully representative of the general population.
edges.rationale: The authors' own generalisability caveat — borrowing their continuum to place a non-student adult is an extrapolation.

edges.quote: there was a significant gender imbalance in our sample, with 81% identifying as women ... our results should be interpreted with caution regarding their generalizability to men
edges.rationale: Response-inhibition findings are the least sex-robust part of the result, and inhibition is exactly the axis the reshaping claim runs through.

edges.quote: Another limitation concerns the exclusive reliance on the ASRS (Kessler et al., 2005; v1.1) for estimating ADHD-like traits. While self-report questionnaires are efficient and widely validated for dimensional studies in the general population, they may lack the precision of multi-instrument or multi-informant approaches.
edges.rationale: The continuum is only as good as the instrument locating people on it — the same instrument this notebook's single data point comes from.
